s: a coin stamped with a spit
6606.full: 1. a small spit , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. a coin stamped with a spit , (Plutarch) 3. the leg of a compass , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6610.full: a loud crying , mostly a joyous cry , in honour of the gods, (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;rarely of lamentation , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

6617.full: to catch scent of, smell, scent, track , with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; absolute, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6622.full: ὁμοιοπαθής, -ές (ὅμοιος, πάσχω), [in LXX: Wis.7:3, 4Ma.12:13 * ;] of like feelings or affections: with dative, Act.14:15, Jas.5:17.† (AS)

6623.full: born of the same mother , Lat. frater uterinus, (Herdotus Historicus); ὁμοματρία ἀδελφή (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6624.full: 1. to be of one mind, agree together, live in harmony , (Thucydides); ὁμονοοῦσα ὀλιγαρχία a united oligarchy, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. with dative to live in harmony with others, with dative, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6626.full: 1. at what point of time, at what hour, on what day , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; ὁπ. ἄν at whatever hour or time , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. in indirect questions, ἢν ὥραν προσήκει ἰέναι, καὶ ὁπ. ἀπιέναι (Aeschines Orator); in answer to a direct question, πηνίκ᾽ ἐστιν τῆς ἡμέρα;—; ὁπηνίκ; what time of day is it? —; what time , do you ask? (Aristophanes Comicus): with genitive, ὁπ. τῆς ὥρας (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in a causal sense, supposing that , ὁπ. ἐφαίνετο ταῦτα πεποιηκώς (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

s: one who teaches the use of arms, a drill-sergeant
6628.full: 1. fighting in heavy arms , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. ὁπλ., one who teaches the use of arms, a drill-sergeant , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

6630.full: ὄζω [in LXX: Exo.8:14 (בָּאַשׁ)* ;] to smell (i.e. emit a smell): Jhn.11:39.† (AS)

6632.full: 1. properly, cooked meat , or, generally, meat , opposite to bread and other provisions, (Homer) 2. anything eaten with bread or food , to give it flavour and relish, κρόμυον, ποτῷ ὄψον onions, a zest or relish to wine, (Iliad by Homer); ἐσθίουσι ἐπὶ τῷ σίτῳ ὄψον (Xenophon Historicus) 3. seasoning, sauce , (Plato Philosophus); κολλύραν καὶ κόνδυλον ὄψον ἐπ᾽ αὐτῇ pudding and knuckle- sauce withal, (Aristophanes Comicus); λιμῷ ὅσαπερ ὄψῳ διαχρῆσθε, i. e. "hunger is the best sauce," (Xenophon Historicus) 4. generally, dainty fare , in plural dainties , (Plato Philosophus) 5. at Athens, mostly, fish , the chief dainty of the Athenians, (Aristophanes Comicus) 6. the fish-market , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6633.full: 1. having the same borders with, marching with, bordering on , τοῖσι Δωριεῦσι, τῇ Λιβύῃ (Herdotus Historicus); absolute bordering , (Thucydides); πόλεμος ὅμορος a border war, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. metaphorically bordering on, closely resembling , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. also as Substantive, a neighbour , (Herdotus Historicus); κατὰ τὸ ὅμορον because of their neighbourhood , (Thucydides) (ML)

6635.full: ὅσπερ, see: ὅς. ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν). __I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), Mrk.15:23, Jhn.5:11; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, Mat.21:35, 22:5, 25:15, Luk.23:33, Act.27:14, Rom.14:5, 1Co.11:21, 2Co.2:18, Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the other, some . . . some, Mat.13:8, 23, Rom.9:21; ὃς (ὃ) μὲν . . . (ἄλλος (ἄλλο)) . . . ἕτερος, Mrk.4:4, Luk.8:5, 1Co.12:8-10; οὓς μέν, absol., 1Co.12:28; ὃς μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, Rom.14:2. __II. As relat. pron., who, which, what, that; __1. agreeing in gender with its antecedent, but differently governed as to case: Mat.2:9, Luk.9:9, Act.20:18, Rom.2:29, al. mult. __2. In variation from the common construction; __(a) in gender, agreeing with a noun in apposition to the antecedent: Mrk.15:16, Gal.3:16, Eph.6:17, al.; constr. ad sensum: Jhn.6:9, Col.2:19, 1Ti.3:16, Rev.13:14, al.; __(b) in number, constr. ad sensum: Act.15:36, 2Pe.3:1; __(with) in case, by attraction to the case of the antecedent (Bl., §50, 2): Jhn.4:18, Act.3:21, Rom.15:18, 1Co.6:19, Eph.1:8, al. __3. The neut. ὅ with nouns of other gender and with phrases, which thing, which term: Mrk.3:17 12:42, Jhn.1:39, Col.3:14, al.; with a sentence, Act.2:32, Gal.2:10, 1Jn.2:8, al. __4. With ellipse of a demonstrative (οὗτος or ἐκεῖνος), before or after: before, Mat.20:23, Luk.7:43, Rom.10:14, al.; after, Mat.10:38, Mrk.9:40, Jhn.19:22, Rom.2:1 al. __5. Expressing purpose, end or cause: Mat.11:10 (who = that he may), Mrk.1:2, Heb.12:6 al. __6. C. prep, as periphrasis for conjc.: ἀνθ᾽ ὧν ( = ἀντὶ τούτων ὧν), because, Luk.1:20, al.; wherefore, Luk.12:3; ἐξ οὗ, since, for that, Rom.5:12; ἀφ᾽ οὗ, since (temporal), Luk.13:25; ἐξ οὗ, whence, Php.3:20; etc. __7. With particles: ὃς ἄν (ἐάν), see: ἄν, ἐάν; ὃς καί, Mrk.3:19, Jhn.21:20, Rom.5:2, al.; ὃς καὶ αὐτός, Mat.27:57. __8. Gen., οὗ, absol., as adv. (see: οὗ). (AS)

s: to rise above, to surpass, excel, have the advantage over
6639.full: 1. to bear or carry over a place, ὑπ. τὸν ἰσθμὸν τὰς ναῦς (Thucydides):—;Pass., [ αἱ ναῦς] αἱ ὑπερενεχθεῖσαι τὸν ἰσθμόν (Thucydides) 2. intransitive to rise above, to surpass, excel, have the advantage over , τινός τινι one in a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); also with accusative pro genitive, ὑπερφέρεις τόλμῃ τόλμαν (Euripides): absolute to excel, have preeminence , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: a stage player, actor . Metaphorical , a pretender, dissembler, hypocrite
6647.full: ὑπο-κριτής, -οῦ, ὁ (ὑποκρίνομαι, which see) [in LXX Job.34:30 36:13 (חָנֵף) * ;] __1. one who answers, an interpreter (Plat.). __2. a stage player, actor (Plut., Xen., al.). Metaphorical (in LXX and NT), a pretender, dissembler, hypocrite: Mat.6:2, 5 6:16 7:5 15:7 22:18 23:13-15 24:51, Mrk.7:6 Luk.6:42 12:56 13:15.† (AS)

6648.full: 1. to be suspicious , (Xenophon Historicus); also, ὑπ. εἴς τινα to have suspicions of him, (Thucydides) 2. to suspect, guess, suppose , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. transitive to suspect, hold in suspicion , (Sophocles Tragicus); ὑπ. τινὰ εἴς τι of something, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be suspected, mistrusted , (Thucydides); impersonal, ὡς ὑπωπτεύετο as was generally suspected , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. with accusative pers. et infinitive to suspect that , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 5. with accusative rei, to look suspiciously on , (Thucydides):—;but also, ὑπ. τι to suspect something, (Euripides) from ὑπόπτης (ML)

6649.full: 1. to fall under or down, to sink in , (Plutarch) 2. to fall down before any one, with accusative, (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, to be subject to him, fall under his power, (Isocrates Orator); of a flatterer, to cringe to , τινί (Demosthenes Orator); with accusative ὑποπεσὼν τὸν δεσπότην (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to fall behind another, (Demosthenes Orator) 4. to get in under or among , (Thucydides) 5. of accidents, to happen, fall out , (Isocrates Orator) 6. of persons, to fall under a punishment, with dative, (Plutarch) 7. of places, to lie under or below , with dative, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

6652.full: ὑπο-χωρέω [in LXX: Jdg.20:37 B (-), Sir.13:9, 2Ma.12:12 * ;] to go back, retire: before ἐν, Luk.5:16; before εἰς, Luk.9:10.† (AS)

s: to lead or bring under, subdue
to go slowly away, withdraw oneself, depart
6654.lxx: in LXX: Exo.14:21 (הָלַךְ hi.), elsewhere only as seel., Tob.8:21, al.
6654.full: ὑπ-άγω [in LXX: Exo.14:21 (הָלַךְ hi.), elsewhere only as seel., Tob.8:21, al. ;] a word of the vulgar language, in Pres. and imperfect only (Bl., § 53, 1). __I. Trans. __1. to lead or bring under, subdue (Hom., Hdt., al.; Ex, l.with). __2. to lead on slowly (Hdt., Xen., al.). __II. Intrans., to go slowly away, withdraw oneself, depart (so less frequently in cl.; Thuc., Eur., al.): absol., Mat.8:32 13:44, Mrk.6:33, Luk.8:42 17:14, Jhn.6:67 8:2 11:44 14:5, 28 18:8; οἱ ἐρχόμενοι κ. οἱ ὑπάγοντες, Mrk.6:31; ὑπῆγον κ. ἐπίστευον, Jhn.12:11; ἵνα ὑπαγῆτε κ. καρπὸν ψέρητε, Jhn.15:16; opposite to ἔρχεσθαι, Jhn.3:8 8:14; imperat., ὕπαγε, Mat.4:10 8:13 20:14, Mrk.2:9 T, Mrk.7:29 10:52; εἰς εἰρήνην (ἐν εἰ.), Mrk.5:34, Jas.2:16; id. prefixed to another imperat. (Bl., § 79, 4), Mat.5:34 8:4 18:15 19:21 21:28 27:65 28:10, Mrk.1:44 10:21 16:7, Jhn.4:16 9:7, Rev.10:8; with καί inserted, Rev.16:1; euphemistically, of death, Mat.26:24, Mrk.14:21; with adv.: ποῦ (which see), Jhn.12:35 14:5 16:5, 1Jn.2:11; ὅπου (which see), Jhn.8:21-22 13:33, 36 14:4 Rev.14:4; ἐκεῖ, Jhn.11:8; with prep.: πρός, Jhn.7:33 13:3 16:5, 10 16:17; εἰς, Mat.9:6 20:4, 7, Mrk.2:11 11:2 14:13, Luk.19:30, Jhn.6:21 7:3 9:11 11:31, Rev.13:10 17:8, 11; εἰς . . . πρός, Mat.26:18, Mrk.5:19; ἐπί, Luk.12:58; μετά, Mat.5:41; ὀπίσω, Mat.16:23, Mrk.8:33; with inf., Jhn.21:3.† (AS)

6655.full: 1. Dep. 2. to lie or be situate above , (Isocrates Orator) 3. to be postponed , (Lucian) (ML)

6656.full: 1. a remembrance, memorial , (Thucydides), etc. 2. a note, memorandum , (Demosthenes Orator):—;in plural memoranda, notes, minutes , Lat. commentarii, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6657.full: ὑπόμινησις, -εως, ἡ (ὑπομιμνήσκω) [in LXX: Psa.71:6 א (תְּהִלָּה), Wis.16:11, 2Ma.6:17 * ;] a reminding, reminder: ἐν ὑ., 2Pe.1:13 3:1; with genitive, 2Ti.1:5.† (AS)

6658.full: 1. indebted, in debt , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὑπ. τινος his debtor , (Plutarch) 2. of property, involved , Lat. obaeratus, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. with genitive, ὑπ. φιλίας bound by ties of friendship, (Plutarch) (ML)

6660.full: carry the neck high, show off

6661.full: the hyaena , an animal of the dog kind, with a bristly mane like a hog (whence the name), (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6671.full: ῥαβδίζω (ῥάβδος), [in LXX: Jdg.6:11 Rut.2:17 (חָבַט) * ;] to beat with a rod: Act.16:22, 2Co.11:25.† (AS)

s: on stated terms, on certain conditions
6673.full: 1. stated, specified , (Iliad by Homer); ἐς χρόνον ῥητόν at a set or stated time, (Herdotus Historicus); ἡμέραι ῥ. (Thucydides); ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς γέρασι with fixed prerogatives, (Thucydides); ῥ. ἀργύριον a stated sum, (Thucydides); ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς on stated terms, on certain conditions , (Herdotus Historicus):—;adverb ῥητῶς, expressly, distinctly , (New Testament) 2. spoken of, known, famous , (Hesiod) 3. that may be spoken or told , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ῥητὸν ἄρρητόν τ᾽ ἔπος, Lat. fas nefasque, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. in Mathem., ῥητά are rational quantities , opposite to surds ἄλογα); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6674.full: to whistle , Lat. stridere, (Iliad by Homer); of a snake, to hiss , (Hesiod):—;Pass. to rush through the air , ἐρροίζητο (3rd singular pluperfect) [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

6675.full: 1. the whistling or whizzing of an arrow, (Iliad by Homer):—;any whistling or piping sound , as of a shepherd, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. rushing motion, a rush, swing , (Plutarch) Formed from the sound. (ML)

6676.full: ῥυπαρός, -ά, -όν (ῥύπος), [in LXX: Zec.3:4-5, (3-4) (צוֹא)* ;] filthy, dirty: of old, shabby clothing (Za, l.with), Jas.2:2; metaphorically, of moral defilement, Rev.22:11.† (AS)

s: anything ridged like the backbone, a mountain-ridge
